prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1274; do not mention it.)
text:
I am writing to advise that this office now represents the injured party in connection with the collision that occurred on the roadway involving your insured. The impact was a low-speed head-on collision, and our client sustained injuries that are being evaluated and treated. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person.

Kindly provide a certified copy of the declarations page for the policy in force at the time of the loss, including the bodily injury and property damage liability limits, along with a statement of any other coverage that may apply, such as umbrella or excess policies. We also ask that your company and your insured preserve all evidence relating to this incident. This includes vehicle data, photographs, witness statements, claim file notes, recorded statements, repair estimates, and any telematics or dashcam footage. Please confirm in writing within fifteen days that this preservation request has been received and acted upon.
